conviction_note: The evidence nets to roughly zero. Third-party traffic data and peer prints point to a comp at or above the top of the 3-4% guide, and the company has beaten its own EPS guide by about $0.20-0.30 in each of the last two quarters. Against that, the bar has moved: the whisper is $1.06 against $0.88 consensus, the stock is up 15% since the last print and up 11.4% over 20 days, and the 25-delta skew is +21.7 vol points put-bid. Record diesel prices in September and October also threaten the Q4 gross-margin guide, and the stock fell 3.9% last quarter on a large beat with a soft guide. So p_up is held at 49 on an 8-point absolute move, and the findings sum (-0.5) and the scaled number (-0.16) agree in sign and are both small.
bar: Q3 FY26 adjusted EPS consensus $0.88 (Earnings Whispers preview, 2026-11-16: https://finviz.com/news/423375/dollar-tree-must-prove-its-210-million-reinvestment-is-buying-traffic-not-just-goodwill), with $0.89 in the sweep row. Revenue consensus is $5.05B. Company guide (2026-08-27: https://corporate.dollartree.com/news-media/press-releases/detail/310): EPS $0.80-0.95 including about $0.50 of tariff-refund reinvestment cost, sales $5.0-5.1B, comps +3-4%, FY26 adjusted EPS $7.70-8.05 including about $0.60 net tariff benefit. Whisper is $1.06. Implied Q4 EPS at the FY midpoint is about $2.56 (my arithmetic: $7.875 FY midpoint less Q1 $1.74, Q2 $2.70 and Q3 midpoint $0.875). print_vs_bar_pct is on EPS: about $1.00-1.05 against $0.88, by analogy with the Q2 beat ($1.39 underlying against a $1.00-1.15 guide) and the Q1 beat ($1.74 against $1.55 consensus). The bar is sourced to the company guide plus two agreeing estimates, so no cap applies.
positioning_check: Short interest: 7.8M shares at the 2026-08-14 settlement, 4.3 days to cover, down from 9.9M on 07-31. That is about 4% of the roughly 191M diluted shares (Curved Trading via search snippet, https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/dltr/short-interest/; the page itself returned 403, so no newer settlement was reachable). This is not a crowded short. Options (sealed baseline): 25-delta skew +21.67 vol points with downside paid; put/call open interest 0.49; event-implied move 8.21%; straddle 9.47%; ATM spread 29% of mid, so the chain is thin. Tape: run-up +11.4% over 20 days and +0.34% over 5 days; 5.3% below the 52-week high. Form 4 prices show $123.65 on 10-27 and $133.87 on 10-31 against a $139.17 spot. Earnings Whispers (11-16) reports bullish sentiment up to 27.3%. Loop Capital downgraded to Hold, PT $140, on 2026-11-05.

findings.finding: Placer.ai (published 2026-11-23) puts Dollar Tree's same-store visits for calendar Q3 2026 (Jul-Sep) at +4.9% YoY, against +1.2% at Dollar General. July alone was +4.8%, so August-September held at about +5% and did not fade. Dollar General had led visit growth for every month of 2026 until July, and the company's own fiscal Q2 (May-Jul) traffic was only +0.4%. Placer visits run above company transaction traffic, but the acceleration after July points to traffic well above Q2's +0.4%. On a ticket trend of about +3%, that implies a Q3 comp at or above the top of the +3-4% guide (consensus sits at the midpoint, $5.05B).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-08-27 a comp beat (3.7% against a 2.5-3.5% guide, with traffic turning positive) plus a large EPS beat drew -3.9%, because the Q3 EPS guide came in 36% below the Street. On 2026-05-28 a beat and FY raise drew +17.9%. The comp line pays only when the guide does not offset it.
findings.why_not_priced: The quarterly figure was published on the day of the seal, after the 11-16 previews that anchor consensus at the comp-guide midpoint. If it were priced, consensus revenue would sit above $5.05B (the guide midpoint) rather than on it. Part of this is already in the price: the July number was public in August, and the +11% 20-day run-up and the $1.06 whisper suggest the buy side expects a beat.
findings.independence: This is a third-party proxy, not a company number. Peer prints over the same Aug-Oct window point the same way (finding 2: https://www.placera.se/pressmeddelanden/ross-stores-ross-stores-reports-strong-third-quarter-sales-and-earnings-results-20261119). July data was corroborated by https://www.credaily.com/briefs/dollar-tree-leads-value-retail-traffic-growth-in-july/?.tsrc=rss, which is the same Placer source.

findings.finding: Value and mass peers covering the same Aug-Oct quarter reported strong traffic-led comps in the week before the print. Ross: Q3 comps +8% against a 6-7% guide, traffic the main driver, Q4 and FY raised (2026-11-19). Target: comps +5.6% with comparable traffic +5.0% and FY sales guide raised, though October slowed (2026-11-18). Walmart US comps were +2.9%, in line, and +3.6% ex-pharmacy (2026-11-19). The low-to-mid-income value shopper was spending through Dollar Tree's fiscal Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not measured for peer read-through on this name. Dollar Tree's own comp beats were bought in May (+17.9%) and sold in August (-3.9%), depending on the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: The peer prints landed after Dollar Tree last spoke (08-27) and after most previews were written. Dollar Tree has issued no in-quarter update (EDGAR shows only an Item 7.01 call-announcement 8-K on 11-03). It is partly priced: DLTR's +11% 20-day run-up overlaps these prints.
findings.independence: Separate companies and documents: Target release https://corporate.target.com/press/release/2026/11/target-corporation-reports-third-quarter-earnings and Walmart coverage https://www.supermarketnews.com/finance/walmart-raises-full-year-outlook-after-strong-third-quarter-sales-ecommerce-growth. These are industry proxies, not Dollar Tree numbers. Target's 'October slowed' cuts slightly against this finding.

findings.finding: The DOE/EIA retail diesel benchmark set an all-time record of $6.285/gal on 2026-09-14, up about $1.71 from $4.578 at the start of July (FreightWaves, 2026-09-15). A mid-October reading was still about $6.28. At the Q2 call management had already flagged 'fuel-driven freight surcharges' and the 10-Q says it expects 'higher freight expenses' in Q3 and Q4. Diesel then rose further after that guide, so the Q3 gross margin ('roughly flat ex tariff items') and the Q4 gross margin (already guided down YoY) both carry freight risk beyond what was guided. That risk bears on the Q4 and FY guide update.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance is the line this name trades on. On 2026-08-27 a 36% Q3 EPS guide shortfall against the Street drew -3.9% despite a large beat; on 2026-05-28 an FY raise drew +17.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: Previews (Earnings Whispers, 11-16) mention freight surcharges only qualitatively, and nothing quantifies the post-guide rise in diesel against Dollar Tree's freight line. If this were priced, the whisper would not sit $0.11 above the top of the EPS guide and the stock would not be within 5% of its 52-week high. The +21.7 put skew may already carry some of it.
findings.independence: The company named the mechanism in the 10-Q filed 2026-08-27 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/935703/000093570326000109/dltr-20260801.htm: 'higher freight expenses' expected in Q3/Q4). The magnitude is macro-to-company inference and the company has not confirmed it. Diesel had also been elevated in May (~$5.60, per the Iran-conflict period noted at https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/gasdiesel/?lv=true), so part of this was in the Aug guide.

findings.finding: The bar has risen above the guide. The whisper is $1.06 against consensus $0.88 and above the $0.95 top of the guide, the stock is up 15.1% since the last report (S&P -1.8%) and about 7% below its post-earnings high of $148.54 (Earnings Whispers, 2026-11-16), and the baseline shows +11.4% over 20 days with +21.7 vol points of put skew. A beat of the published consensus is expected, so the reaction turns on the Q4 and FY guide.

findings.why_not_priced: This is the priced state, filed so the panel sees it. The open question is whether the market has paid for more than the whisper. Short interest is about 4% of shares, so no squeeze mechanism offsets it.
findings.independence: The sealed baseline (run_up_20d +11.41, skew +21.67) is independent of the Earnings Whispers article. It shares the EW document with the bar field.

findings.finding: The 10-Q lists open AD/CVD exposure: retroactive duties of up to about $11M on aluminum pans and about $15M on paper plates (final determination due 2026-10-14, inside Q3), plus a new circumvention inquiry on Malaysian and Indonesian aluminum pans. The company says a loss is not probable. A Q3 charge would be a one-off of at most about $0.10/share pre-tax.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 $13M duty charge sat inside the tariff bucket and drew no separate reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: It is buried in a 10-Q legal note and small. It is sized as a one-off with no path to the guide.
findings.independence: None. Shares the 10-Q with findings 3 and 5.

baseline_tension: The traffic and peer evidence leans up and cuts against the +21.7 put skew. The bar evidence (whisper above the guide top, +11% run-up) and the diesel-to-freight risk agree with the skew. Net, the findings are close to zero, so I do not take a side against the option market.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a fact is not a reaction): the Placer comp finding went from +1.0 to +0.8, because this name sold a comp and EPS beat in August on the guide.

Lesson 5 (proxy vs company number): the peer read-through went from +0.5 to +0.4 as an industry proxy. The diesel finding went from -1.0 to -0.8, because the magnitude is macro-to-company inference, though the company did name the mechanism.

Lesson 7 (positioning): the run-up/whisper finding went from -0.8 to -0.6 because it agrees with the put skew and is likely already priced. Short interest (about 4%) was checked before keeping any negatives; it is not crowded.

Lesson 6 (bar): the bar is sourced to the company guide plus two agreeing estimates ($0.88 and $0.89), so no cap applies. Nothing in the findings resolves after the window except the circumvention item, which went to outside_window.
